0.4.0.lead: Your nex apps now work together: connect nextime with nextasks, nexpaper, nexmail, nexdiary and nexnotes with one click, without typing keys. Also new: passkeys, more control over AI tools, and settings as in every nex app.

sections.title: Connect apps with one click
sections.body: Until now you made an API key in the other app and typed it in here. Now each app has a card of its own: click “Connect with …”, sign in to the other app and agree once, done. The consent page shows which account is signed in and what each side may do, in words like “Tick tasks off”. When an app may read your calendars, you choose which ones. One consent covers both directions, and each app may do only what it really needs. The card shows since when you are connected, when the connection was last used and what is allowed; “Check now” and “Disconnect” (for both sides) are right there. If something goes wrong, you land back in your card and read there what happened. Connections made with a key keep working as before and can be renewed the new way.

sections.title: nextasks and nexpaper in the calendar
sections.body: Due tasks from nextasks, yours and those assigned to you, show in Today, Day, Week, Month and the lists. Tick them off right in the calendar, and choose which areas and lists appear. Open deadlines from nexpaper, such as paying, cancelling by or a warranty, stand as all-day entries on the day you have to act by; a click opens the document in nexpaper. Both were there before, now connected with one click.

sections.title: A note for an event in nexnotes
sections.where: Open an event › Note in nexnotes
sections.body: New: “Note in nexnotes” puts a note with the event's title, time, place and notes into the nexnotes inbox with one click, for points on a meeting, say. The same event never gets a second one; nextime tells you the note is already there. The button appears once nextime is connected with nexnotes.

sections.title: Your calendars in nexmail and nexdiary
sections.body: nexmail shows all your calendars from nextime with their groups and colors, makes an event in nextime from a mail, enters invitations from mails and answers them. That was there before, now connected with one click. New is nexdiary: while you write up a day, it shows that day's events from nextime to look back on. nexdiary only reads. You choose which calendars the two see when you connect.

sections.title: AI tools that ask first
sections.where: Settings › My account › Connections › AI tools (MCP)
sections.body: Connect AI programs with an MCP key of their own, or with no key at all: the program signs itself in, you agree once and choose what it may do and which calendars it reaches. Under “Rights per tool” you set each tool to Allow, Ask or Deny. When a program asks, nextime tells your browsers that have notifications on; a tap opens the request, and you allow or decline. API keys with the box for AI tools keep working.

sections.title: Sign in with a passkey
sections.body: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or the PIN of your device, without a password. Passkeys need the public address with https. Usernames are new too: you sign in with your username or your email. Forgot your password? nextime mails you a link once the operator has set up mail. A new email address is confirmed by a link.

sections.title: Settings as in every nex app
sections.body: The same areas, cards and buttons as in the other nex apps. In Appearance you choose Light, Dark or As the system, now for your account on every device. “Reminders” is now “Notifications” and starts with the ways: notifications for this browser, a test notification, iPhone and iPad. Connections brings devices, installing, the other apps, API keys and AI tools to one place; keys can be edited now. For the operator, “Other nex apps” and “Interfaces” stand under Server › Connections.

sections.title: Backups every week or every month
sections.body: Besides “Every night” there are “Every week” and “Every month”. “Back up now” takes a note along that stands beside the backup in the list. The card “Storage” shows how much nextime takes and what is still free.

sections.title: Ready for the iPhone and iPad app
sections.body: “Connect iPhone or iPad” shows a QR code that is valid for 10 minutes; without a camera you sign in from the app as in the browser. The card “Devices” lists every connected device, and “Disconnect” locks one out at once. The app keeps every event on the device, also without a connection, and brings what was entered to the server exactly once afterwards; after a conflict you see both versions. The app itself comes separately.

small: Invite attendees to events in iCloud and Google calendars by their email address. iCloud or Google sends the invitation as usual, and the answers of those invited are kept. nextime's own calendars invite nobody.

The operator enters the addresses of the other nex apps once under Server › Connections › Other nex apps and allows connections into the local network there when needed; after that every account connects with one click.

Under Server › Connections › Interfaces the operator decides whether AI programs may connect themselves, the highest level and blocked tools. On a new installation MCP starts off; where it was on, it stays on.
“Ready for the internet?” under Server › Sign-in checks https, the second factor, the brake on guessing, cookies, the proxy and whether the server reaches the internet, and says what to do.
Only the operator sees whether a new version is out; a new installation asks once whether nextime should look.
Under Server › Accounts the operator sees every API key and can lock single ones; expired invitations stay listed there until withdrawn.
System mail goes out right after saving, and the log blacks out every key and every guest link.
The time zone is in the profile now, under the language. There is no storage limit per account any more; the limit per file stays.
Set up the calendar account from the app on the same iPhone, and only the app reminds there. Notifications of changes in shared calendars reach the app too.
Fixed: nextime now also starts in a container with tightly cut rights; until now the start stopped at the write test of the data folder.

0.3.0.lead: A year at a glance, a new overview of the coming weeks and a tidier sidebar.

sections.title: The year as a heat map
sections.body: The twelve months on one page, each day a field, the stronger the more is going on. Full weeks and free stretches show at once. A click on a day opens it, a click on a month's name opens the month. The year fits the screen without scrolling.

sections.title: Upcoming
sections.body: On top what comes next and how full the next 14 days are, with the next calm stretch. Below, the coming weeks as columns side by side, with the free days between them; “Later” shows whole days and holidays only. The chips on top choose what you see, as the collection does.

sections.title: Today, Calendar, Upcoming
sections.body: The sidebar now holds places: the “Today” overview, “Calendar” and “Upcoming”. Day, week, month or year is chosen on top only; “Calendar” opens the view you had last. A click on a calendar in the sidebar stays in the view you are in.

sections.title: Events in the month in color
sections.body: Under “Events in the month” choose between the dot in the calendar's color and a row tinted in it.

small: A click on a day in the month or on “+ n more” opens the day; a new event comes from the “+” in the corner of the day.
Pages load without flicker, and the month opens much faster.
The column of coming events stands beside the year too, as beside the other views.

0.2.0.lead: Holidays from iCloud, Google or a subscription now stand out just like the built-in ones, and nexmail can read your calendars and enter invitations from mails.

sections.title: Highlight its days
sections.body: A background calendar can tint its days, as holidays do. So a holiday calendar from iCloud, Google or a subscription stands out too. The box “Highlight its days” sits under “Show in the background” and is yours alone. The built-in public holidays are highlighted from the start, school holidays are not.

sections.title: For nexmail
sections.body: With a key for nextime, nexmail groups your calendars as they are grouped here, sees whether an invitation is already entered, answers it and enters invitations from a mail. nextime sends nothing itself, so the answer goes out exactly once. When the same event comes from iCloud or Google later, it still stands only once.

small: The API names each event's UID and its address in nextime, and the organizer and attendees.
Hidden calendars appear in the API marked as hidden; a program reads their events only when it asks for them by name.
Mail copies of an invitation show no answer buttons in nextime; the trash says why an event went there.

0.1.0.lead: The first version of nextime: your calendars on your own server, in the browser and through CalDAV on iPhone and Android. A short tour of what is already there.

sections.title: Today, day, week and month
sections.body: “Today” shows what comes next and how soon, the rest of the day below it and the events of the coming days beside it. The week has the column “Coming up” on the right, which folds away. Events move by dragging, and the keys T, W, M and H switch to day, week, month and today.

sections.title: Calendars of your own
sections.body: Add as many calendars as you need, each with one of eleven colors or one of your own and a symbol. Show and hide them and put them in your own order. Events are all-day or have a time and time zone, are busy or free, and repeat daily, weekly, monthly or yearly, with exceptions too.

sections.title: Sharing with people and by link
sections.body: Share a calendar with others on your server, each person with a right of their own: busy only, read or edit. Guests without an account get a link to read, which they can also subscribe to. In a shared calendar a picture shows who entered an event, and if you like, nextime tells you when others change something.

sections.title: iCloud, Google, CalDAV and subscriptions
sections.body: Bring in your calendars from iCloud, Google or another CalDAV server such as Nextcloud, to read and write, synced every minute. What you change while a source is away goes out later. Subscriptions to calendar links come along, and public and school holidays of Germany, Austria and Switzerland are built in, without asking any outside service. Invitations from iCloud and Google are answered right in nextime.

sections.title: Calendar account for iPhone and Android
sections.where: Settings › My account › On iPhone and co
sections.body: Through CalDAV your calendars show in Apple Calendar, on Android with DAVx5 and in Thunderbird. Every device gets a password of its own and can be locked out on its own; the iPhone scans a QR code and loads a profile. This needs nextime reached over HTTPS.

sections.title: Reminders, place and attachments
sections.where: Open an event; Settings › My account › Notifications
sections.body: Reminders are yours alone and can be set per device. A place gets address suggestions and a small map, notes may hold links, and an event takes attachments. “Join” takes you into a video meeting.

sections.title: Quick entry and defaults per calendar
sections.where: Today, at the top; a calendar's menu › Edit …
sections.body: A line like “Tomorrow 3 pm dentist” becomes an event with day and time. Every calendar can have defaults for new events, such as an all-day yearly birthday with a reminder the day before.

sections.title: Search and trash
sections.body: Search goes over every calendar and opens anywhere with Ctrl K or “/”. What you delete goes to the trash and comes back from there, and right after deleting with “Undo” too.

sections.title: Tasks and deadlines in the calendar
sections.body: Due tasks from nextasks and deadlines from nexpaper stand in your calendar. Each person connects them on their own, with a key of that app.

sections.title: Take along and move
sections.where: Settings › My account › Take along and move
sections.body: Every calendar downloads as an ICS file, all of them together as a ZIP with the attachments. An ICS file goes into a calendar of your own with a preview and without duplicates. A calendar from iCloud or Google moves into one of your own, while everything there stays as it is.

sections.title: API and MCP
sections.body: With a key of your own, programs read your calendars and, if you want, add events: through the REST API or as an MCP server for AI tools. Every key has rights of its own, and the operator decides who may use them.

small: Light, dark or like the device.
German and English; the operator adds more languages as files.
The first day of the week, week numbers, 12 or 24 hours and the time zone are set per account.
nextime installs from the browser as an app. On a phone the week shows three days, with a bar at the bottom.
Without a connection the installed app keeps showing the next four weeks to read and search; adding events needs a connection again.
